highlightSectionTitle: Why the C5 is the OLED most people should buy

highlights.title: Picture quality within a hair of the flagships
highlights.body: The C5's OLED evo panel delivers the perfect blacks and near-infinite contrast OLED is known for, and in a normally lit living room most viewers cannot tell it from LG's step-up models without side-by-side comparison. It gets bright enough for daytime sports and keeps its colour punch in HDR — you are paying twice as much elsewhere for diminishing returns.

highlights.title: A genuinely good gamer TV
highlights.body: Four full-bandwidth HDMI 2.1 ports, 4K at 144Hz for PC players, near-instant response times and support for both major VRR flavors make the C5 one of the best gaming displays at any price. PS5 and Xbox Series X owners lose essentially nothing gaming on a C5 versus a TV that costs far more.

highlights.title: webOS keeps improving, and the C6 is not a reason to wait
highlights.body: The generational refresh to the C6 brings a modest brightness bump and a new design, not a picture-quality revolution. Buying the C5 at its discounted floor — the live table below — gets you about 95% of the experience with money left over for a soundbar, which a flat TV badly needs.

adviceSectionTitle: How to pay the least without getting burned
advicePoints: Size is the biggest price lever: the 65" usually offers the best price-per-inch when discounted, while the 48" carries a premium for its size class. Check the live table across sizes before assuming bigger costs proportionally more.

Buy on the retail calendar: the deepest C5 cuts historically land around Super Bowl season, Prime Day, and Black Friday–Cyber Monday. Outside those windows, Best Buy price-matches Amazon on identical SKUs — ask, it works.

Check the panel at delivery. OLED panels are fragile in transit; unbox on video, run a full-grey test slide for dead pixels and vertical banding within the return window, and exchange immediately rather than living with it.
Costco members should price the Concierge bundle: the 90-day return window and second-year coverage effectively extend your safety net on a TV category where a bad panel is the main risk.

Do not pay extra for extended burn-in coverage you likely will not use: modern OLEDs vary pixel brightness and run compensation cycles automatically. Burn-in is a risk for constant static-content displays, not typical mixed TV, movie and gaming use.
faqSectionTitle: LG C5 OLED in the US — common questions

faqs.question: Is the LG C5 worth buying in 2026, or should I wait for the C6?
faqs.answer: For most buyers, buy the C5. The C6 is an incremental brightness and design refresh, while the C5's discount — visible in the live prices on this page — buys a soundbar or a games console with the difference. Only videophiles who want the newest panel should pay the early-adopter premium.

faqs.question: What's the best price on an LG C5 right now?
faqs.answer: The live table on this page shows the current floor across US retailers and sizes, refreshed continuously. Prices move most around Super Bowl, Prime Day and Black Friday; between events, Best Buy will typically price-match Amazon's dips on identical models.

faqs.question: Which LG C5 size is the best value?
faqs.answer: The 65-inch usually has the best price-per-inch when discounted and suits most living rooms at typical viewing distances. The 48-inch is best for desks and small rooms but costs more per inch; the 77-inch carries a steep premium for home-theatre setups.

faqs.question: Should I worry about OLED burn-in on the C5?
faqs.answer: For normal mixed use — streaming, sports, gaming — no. The C5 runs automatic compensation cycles and varies static-element brightness. Burn-in is mostly a risk for displays that show the same static interface all day, like news tickers or a PC taskbar, for years.

faqs.question: Is the LG C5 good for PS5 or Xbox Series X gaming?
faqs.answer: Yes — it is one of the best gaming TVs at any price. Four HDMI 2.1 ports, 4K/120 (144Hz for PC), VRR support and near-instant pixel response make it a natural pairing for current consoles.

categoryIntro.heading: Why LG C5 prices vary so much across US retailers
categoryIntro.body: Big-screen TVs are the most aggressively competitive category in US electronics retail: the same C5 SKU is listed at any given moment by Best Buy, Amazon, Walmart, Costco, Adorama and B&H at prices that diverge by hundreds of dollars and reshuffle every time one of them blinks first. Add size-dependent pricing and open-box units, and a static 'best TV deal' article is stale before it is published — which is why this page reads live listings across all of them instead.
